title: Conditions of Device Issue under the Student Technology Device Program
content:
## Conditions of issue

1. A device of the Student Technology Device Program is checked out only to a student whose district enrollment record for the school year is in status provisional or enrolled, at that record's campus.
2. The parent must have signed the device loan agreement and the student and parent must have acknowledged the acceptable use policy, both through the family portal, before checkout.
3. The loan type must admit the student's grade; Windows laptop loans are for students enrolled in a career and technical education course that requires one.
4. A device whose service year exceeds the device service life of 4 years is retired and never checked out.

## The conditions read one by one

| Condition | What shows it | Met when |
|---|---|---|
| Enrollment | The student's district enrollment record for the school year, as held on Student Enrollment, Transfers and Pre-Kindergarten Admissions | The record is in status provisional or enrolled; the device is issued at that record's campus |
| Agreement | The family portal | The parent has signed the device loan agreement before checkout |
| Acceptable use | The family portal | The student and the parent have both acknowledged the acceptable use policy before checkout |
| Grade | The loan type's grade list | The student's grade is on the loan type's list |
| Windows laptop | The student's course enrollment | The student is enrolled in a career and technical education course that requires a Windows laptop |
| Device age | The device's service year | The service year does not exceed 4 |

The enrollment condition is read from the district's system record, before the checkout, for the same student; a statement by the family does not stand in for it.

## Hypothetical cases

- A hypothetical student whose enrollment record for the school year is in status provisional, at a given campus, meets the enrollment condition for a device issued at that campus.
- A hypothetical device in service year 4 is within the 4-year service life; a device in service year 5 exceeds it, is retired and is never checked out.
- A hypothetical household in which the parent has signed the device loan agreement but the student has not yet acknowledged the acceptable use policy has not met the second condition, which requires both acknowledgments before checkout.
